sec:
Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in Idaho, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Ask for your ballot by

Friday, October 23Passed

Your request must reach your county clerk before 5 p.m. local time on Friday, October 23, 2026. (official page)

Send it back by

Tuesday, November 3Passed

Your ballot must be back at your county elections office by 8 p.m. on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026, to be counted. (official page)

The last day to ask for a ballot by mail has passed. You can still vote in person, early or on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.You can still vote in person on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. Early voting in person runs through Friday, October 30, 2026. When and where to vote early.

Ask for a ballot online, on Idaho’s own site

At school away from home, in Idaho or in another state? What Idaho says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

Any registered Idaho voter can ask for an absentee ballot to be mailed to them. You do not have to give a reason. (official page)

How to ask for a ballot

  • Online. Request it on the state's voter website. You need your Idaho driver's license or state ID number and the last four digits of your Social Security number. You do not have to scan anything. Open it (official page)
  • By mail. Print the state's absentee ballot application, check the November 3, 2026 box, sign it by hand, and send it to your county clerk (the addresses are printed on the form). Electronic signatures are not accepted. Open it (official page)
  • In person. You can also vote absentee in person at your county's early voting location (see early voting below). (official page)

How to send it back

  • By mail. Mail it in the return envelope. You need to add a stamp. (official page)
  • Drop box. Put it in an official elections drop box. (official page)
  • In person. Bring it to your county elections office. (official page)

What the envelope needs

Sign the outside of the return envelope; elections staff check every signature. A new request is needed each calendar year. (official page)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on Idaho’s own site (official page)

Vote early in person instead

Tuesday, October 13, 2026 to Friday, October 30, 2026.

Early voting (in-person absentee) is open in every county through Friday, October 30, 2026. Start dates differ by county: October 13 in most counties, October 14 in Power County, and October 19 in others, including Ada, Bonneville, Canyon and Kootenai. Ask your county clerk for places and hours. (official page)

Students

At school in Idaho, away from home

The state says students should register at the address they consider home, whether that is their college address or another address. You may be registered in only one place. The state warns that changing your declared residence may affect scholarships or stipends. An enrollment letter from an Idaho university is accepted as proof of where you live when you register. (official page)

At school in another state, with Idaho as home

The state's pages do not speak separately to Idaho students at school in another state. Its general rule (Idaho Code 34-107) is that a voter who leaves home for a temporary purpose, to another state or another Idaho county, does not lose their Idaho residence; a voter who moves to another state meaning to make it their permanent home does. (the law)

Military and overseas

Military voters and U.S. citizens living abroad can register and request a ballot online, or send the Federal Post Card Application to their county elections office. The ballot comes by mail or as an email link; print it, mark it, sign it and mail it back. Requests must arrive by 5 p.m. on the 11th day before the election (October 23, 2026), and ballots by 8 p.m. on Election Day. (official page)

Idaho in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • The request deadline is two days away as of October 21, 2026: before 5 p.m. local time on Friday, October 23. After that, you can still vote in person at an early voting location through October 30, or at your polling place on Election Day.
  • The state's pages do not say whether someone else may drop off your ballot for you; ask your county clerk.
Where this comes from: 5 pages of Idaho’s election office, its laws and the federal guide

  2. Absentee Ballot Application, 2026 calendar year (EA-5, revised 03/31/2026), Idaho Secretary of State (official page; read October 21, 2026)
  3. 2026 Idaho General Election, Idaho Secretary of State (VoteIdaho) (official page; read October 21, 2026)
  4. Student and Residency Voting, Idaho Secretary of State (VoteIdaho) (official page; read October 21, 2026)
  5. Idaho Code 34-107, "Residence" defined, Idaho Legislature (the law; read October 21, 2026)

Checked October 21, 2026. Rules and dates can change: Idaho’s election office, and your county or local election office, have the final word.

polls:
Polls are open 8 a.m. (7 a.m. in some counties) to 8 p.m. local time. (the law)

  • rest of the state: 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. MST
  • Northern Idaho, north of the Salmon River: 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. PST

Anyone in line when the polls close may still vote.
